slides.slide_text_ocr:
Operator Composition

each operator produces a set (bag/stream) of result tuples

operators consume zero or more input sets

usually assume nothing about their input

therefore can be combined in an arbitrary manner

very flexible

slides.title: Operator Interface
slides.chapter_header: Sire Ol -lammcesiiam Set-Oriented Query Processing
slides.slide_text_ocr:
Operator Interface

Option 1: Full Materialization

Every operator materializes its output. The input is always read from a materialized state

Advantages:

e easy to implement

e can handle surprises concerning intermediate result sizes

(dynamic plans)

e advanced techniques like parallelization, result sharing, etc. are simple

Disadvantages:

e materialization is expensive

e in particular if data is larger than main memory

-™rei

slides.title: Operator Interface (2)
slides.chapter_header: Sire Ol -lammcesiiam Set-Oriented Query Processing
slides.slide_text_ocr:
Operator Interface (2)

Option 2: Iterator Model

Each operator produces a tuple stream on demand. The input is iterated over.

Advantages:

e

data is pipelined between operators

e

avoids unnecessary materialization

e

flexible control flow

e

easy to implement

Disadvantages:

e millions of virtual function calls

e poor locality

slides.slide_text_ocr:
Operator Interface (5)

Option 3: blockwise processing

Each operator produces a tuple stream, but not tuple-by-tuple but as a stream of larger chunks.

Advantages:

e far fewer function calls

e better code and data locality

Disadvantages:

e additional materialization overhead

® consumes memory bandwidth

e control flow not as flexible

slides.chapter_header: Sire Ol -lammcesiiam Set-Oriented Query Processing
slides.slide_text_ocr:
Operator Interface (6)

Option 4: pushing tuples up

Each operator pushes produced tuples towards the consuming operators

Advantages:

e

operator logic is concentrated in a few loops

e

good code and data locality

e

pipelining etc. still possible

e

support for DAG-structured plans

Disadvantages:

e some restrictions in control flow

e code generation more involved

slides.title: Pipelining
slides.chapter_header: Sire Ol -lammcesiiam Set-Oriented Query Processing
slides.slide_text_ocr:
Pipelining

As mentioned, most approaches try to avoid copying data between operators

e this is called pipelining

© operators that do materialize their input are called pipeline breakers

© operators are consume their input completely before processing are called full pipeline

breakers

e some binary operators are pipeline breakers on only one side

This behavior has implications regarding other operators.

slides.title: Pipelining (2)
slides.chapter_header: Sire Ol -lammcesiiam Set-Oriented Query Processing
slides.slide_text_ocr:
Pipelining (2)

Some effects of different pipeline behavior

e if a pipeline break is between source and sink the original data is no longer accessible

> relevant for lazy attribute access/TID join/string representations etc.

P the system must plan defensively

e if a full pipeline breaker is between two operators both are decoupled

> the full pipeline break breaks the plan into fragments

P can be executed independent from each other

> relevant for scheduling

The code generation must know the pipeline behavior of operators.

slides.title: Parallelization
slides.chapter_header: Sire Ol -lammcesiiam Set-Oriented Query Processing
slides.slide_text_ocr:
Parallelization

How can we exploit multiple cores during query processing?

e inter-query parallelism is simple

e intra-query parallelism is much harder

e independent parts of the query can be executed in parallel (see: full pipeline breaker)

e parallelizing individual operators is more difficult

e usual strategy: partition the input

We will discuss this later in more detail.

Idea: non-inner joins mark tuples with a join partner
